purpose: One identity for each recurring Potatoism concept. Lexicons, cosmology tables, maps, timelines and relationship files are projections or evidence layers; they must not create a second identity for the same concept.

rules.one_identity: A recurring concept has one canonical_id.
rules.aliases: Alternative spellings, titles and compound forms resolve to the same canonical_id when they describe the same project concept.
rules.occurrences: Source occurrences remain available for provenance, but the repository index collapses them into one navigational concept.
rules.relationships: A relationship such as Father → Son is an edge, not another Father or Son record.
rules.distinctness: Concepts that are genuinely different remain separate even when they share words; Father, Father’s House and Father → Son are not the same kind of record.
rules.evidence: Comparative or historical material must remain visibly separate from project-defined mythology.

concepts.definition: The Father is the originating/source-side archetype of the Potatoverse: the upper pole of the Father–Son relation, associated with origin, generative authority, orientation and the conditions from which the lower world can develop.

The Father's House is the dwelling/chamber metaphor associated with the Father-side of the architecture. The project's thalamus correspondence is a metaphorical analogy, not scientific evidence for the cosmology.

Source names the originating principle or depth from which a relation, structure or sequence proceeds. It is broader than Father: Father is an archetypal figure within the mythology, while Source describes the generative relation itself.

Heaven is the project's upper/sourceward orientation: a symbolic direction of transcendence, origin, perspective and relation rather than a scientifically mapped physical location. Its meaning changes with context, so it should not be duplicated into several separate 'heaven' identities.

The Son is the embodied counterpart of the Father-side: the participant who enters the Plane, experiences separation and strife, and functions through the connected images of Door, Vessel and Ladder. Historical names remain comparative references unless explicitly marked as such.

The Door is the boundary/interface through which distinct domains can meet. It is not merely an exit: its key question is what crosses the boundary, what remains distinct, and whether the passage creates understanding.

The Ladder is the traversable form of vertical connection: levels become a route rather than a static hierarchy. In the project's symbolic sequence, the Door can become a Ladder when a boundary becomes a usable connection.

The North Axis is the orienting spine of the mythology. North functions as direction, extremity and symbolic orientation; Axis names the relation that keeps the system from becoming a pile of disconnected symbols.

The Tree of Life models continuity between hidden foundation and visible outcome: root, trunk, branch, fruit and seed form a regenerative cycle in which what is received can become future nourishment.
The Tree of Strife is the failure-mode counterpart to the Tree of Life: attention and resources circulate through conflict, extraction, fear and repetition without regenerative return.
The Potato of Life is the grounded-life symbol at the center of the mythology: hidden potential, nourishment, roots, persistence, reproduction and growth emerging from ordinary matter.
Mud is the messy, material starting condition from which roots can begin. It is not pure evil or a permanent identity; its significance depends on whether something is actually growing through it.
The Swamp is a systems metaphor for accumulated muddiness, incentives, institutional entanglement and unresolved dependencies. It is not a literal hidden organization.
Spudlight names illumination discovered through grounded life: meaning becomes visible inside ordinary matter rather than requiring the ordinary world to be discarded.
